query: zapier vs make vs n8n for a small team
title: Zapier vs Make vs n8n for a small team | 50agents
description: Zapier vs Make vs n8n for a small team: Zapier is quickest to learn, Make shows branching visually, n8n charges per run and can self-host.
h1: Zapier vs Make vs n8n for a small team
answer: Pick Zapier for the quickest start and the most apps, Make if your workflows branch and you like to see them as a diagram, and n8n if someone on the team is technical and you want to pay per run or host it yourself.
The way each counts usage (tasks, credits, executions) matters more to your bill than the headline price.

rows: Several non-technical people will build; you use niche apps; you want help docs for everything. It is where most app makers build their integration first.
Your workflows branch, loop over lists and handle errors in specific ways, and someone on the team likes to see the whole flow.
You have someone comfortable with JSON and a little code; your workflows have many steps (so per-run pricing wins); or your data must stay on your own server.

body.p: Where each is better, plainly: Zapier has the most apps and the gentlest start. Make gives the most control per dollar for visual builders. n8n is the only one of the three you can run yourself, and its per-run pricing is far cheaper for long workflows.

Take a workflow that runs 600 times a month: a trigger, a lookup and an add-row step. For each plan’s price, see [how much automation costs](/guides/how-much-automation-costs-credits-tasks-and-runs-compared).

method.h2: How to choose in an afternoon

steps.title: Write your three most likely workflows
steps.body: The apps, the trigger, the steps, and how often each runs a month.

steps.title: Check every app is supported
steps.body: Search each tool’s app directory for each app, and for the specific trigger and action you need, not just the app name.

steps.title: Work out the monthly units
steps.body: Tasks, credits or executions, using the rules above. This usually decides it.

steps.title: Build the hardest one on each free tier
steps.body: Branching, a loop over line items, an error case. An hour each is enough to feel the difference.

steps.title: Ask who will fix it at 7:00 on a Monday
steps.body: Pick the tool that person can read.

body: 50agents is a different shape: you do not build the steps, you tell Captain the job and it plans the automation, an AI agent, a browser agent or an app, through viaSocket’s 2,300+ apps. If you enjoy building flows and want every setting in your hands, the three tools above give you more control. If you would rather describe the job, check the plan, and approve what reaches customers, try the same workflow there.

wrong.title: The bill is not the headline price
wrong.body: Usage beyond the plan is where costs grow. Count your units before choosing.

wrong.title: Polling uses credits
wrong.body: A trigger that checks every few minutes can spend credits on empty checks in some tools. Use instant triggers where offered.

wrong.title: Self-hosting is not free
wrong.body: n8n on your own server costs the server and someone’s time for updates and backups.

wrong.title: Nobody can read the flow
wrong.body: The builder leaves and the diagram is a mystery. Name steps in plain words and keep a one-line note per workflow.

wrong.title: Quotas stop your workflows
wrong.body: When credits or tasks run out, workflows stop. Set alerts before the limit.

faqs.a: Self-hosted n8n is free to use; you pay for the server and the upkeep. n8n cloud is paid, with a trial.

faqs.q: Which is cheapest for a small team?
faqs.a: It depends on workflow length. For long workflows n8n’s per-run pricing is usually cheapest; for short two-step jobs the free tiers of Zapier or Make may cover you.
Zapier, for most non-technical people. Make is a step up in control; n8n another step.
